source: Nisbett, Peng, Choi, Norenzayan (2001) Culture and systems of thought: holistic versus analytic cognition, Psychological Review 108
finding: The founding paper is a review that proposes a theory. It pulls together many studies and claims East Asians and Westerners differ in kind, not only in degree.
numbers: Review of many studies, no pooled N. It says differences are 'qualitatively different'; for example Americans show a large primacy effect in covariation judgments and Chinese show none.
quote: responded in qualitatively different ways to the same stimulus situation in study after study
limits: A synthesis of mostly small student samples, usually two or three countries. It gives no pooled effect size.
agent_relevance: The claim 'different cognitive systems' is the strongest form of the idea. Later work (b05, b07, b08) supports only a weaker, task-by-task version.

source: Nisbett, Peng, Choi, Norenzayan (2001) Culture and systems of thought: holistic versus analytic cognition, Psychological Review 108
finding: Covariation detection (Ji, Peng, Nisbett): Chinese judged more association between arbitrary figures, were more confident, and were better calibrated. Americans showed a primacy effect, Chinese did not.
numbers: True covariation ranged from r=.00 to .60 in the stimuli. N not given in the review.
limits: Read through the review, not in the original study.
agent_relevance: Order effects (primacy) differed by group. A reasoning scaffold should not assume one order bias for every framing.

source: Nisbett, Peng, Choi, Norenzayan (2001) Culture and systems of thought: holistic versus analytic cognition, Psychological Review 108
finding: Triad grouping (Ji and Nisbett): Chinese students grouped by relationship (the sun is in the sky). Americans grouped by category (both are in the heavens) and justified it the same way.
numbers: Verbal triads in native language. Sample sizes not given in the review.
limits: Group-level tendency. Later work shows the triad task is only weakly related to other style tasks (b05).
agent_relevance: Two valid framings of the same set: relation-based and category-based. Supports O6 and O8 (try the other framing).

source: Nisbett, Peng, Choi, Norenzayan (2001) Culture and systems of thought: holistic versus analytic cognition, Psychological Review 108
finding: Typicality effect in argument strength (Norenzayan, Choi, Nisbett): Koreans were more convinced by typical-instance arguments. European Americans rated typical and atypical arguments as equal. Asian Americans fell in between.
numbers: Three groups. The effect changed when typicality information was made salient (all three groups then showed it).
quote: When an experimental manipulation was introduced that increased the salience of the typicality information
limits: A boundary condition inside the review: the difference depends on how salient the information is.
agent_relevance: The logic-versus-intuition split is a default that shifts with presentation. A scaffold can steer it by how the task is shown.

source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Kitayama, Gonzalez, Nisbett (2010) Cultural differences are not always reducible to individual differences, PNAS 107(14)
finding: Ten cognitive-style measures (triad, framed line, proverbs, attribution, change sensitivity and others) barely correlate with each other within a group, even though each one separates cultures.
numbers: Mean r=0.038, median r=0.040 across the 10 cognitive-style measures. First factor explains 10.69% of variance (chance is 10%). Excluding measures with alpha<0.60: mean r=0.031, median 0.072. For comparison, WAIS subtests average r=0.48.
limits: The measures were chosen for their success at separating cultures. The authors say poor reliability does not explain the result.
agent_relevance: Analytic-holistic is not one trait. It is a bundle of weakly linked habits. A scaffold should not label a model or user 'holistic' and switch everything.

source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Kitayama, Gonzalez, Nisbett (2010) Cultural differences are not always reducible to individual differences, PNAS 107(14)
finding: Published cultural effect sizes for these tasks are moderate to large. Social class also shifts holism, again without internal coherence.
numbers: Mean Cohen's d=0.62 for cognitive style (0.54 for social orientation), taken from published East Asian vs Western studies. Working class more holistic on 7 of 10 measures, 5 significant, 1 significant the other way. Aggregate class difference t(213)=3.51, p<.001.
limits: The d values come from published studies, which may be inflated by publication bias. Nothing here tests that.
agent_relevance: Style varies with social class and experience, not only nation. It is a context-dependent habit, so a prompt or task could induce it.

source: Evans, Rotello, Li, Rayner (2009) Scene perception and memory revealed by eye movements and ROC analyses: does a cultural difference truly exist? QJEP 62(2)
finding: A failed replication of the claim (Chua et al. 2005) that Chinese viewers look more at the background. Eye movements and recognition memory were the same for Americans and Chinese.
numbers: 22 Americans and 22 Chinese graduate students (mean ages 25.6 and 26.9), EyeLink 1000. Both groups made longer and more fixations on focal objects than on context. The accuracy drop and bias shift when an object was tested in a new context did not differ by culture.
quote: both Americans and Chinese use the same strategies in scene perception and memory
limits: Small sample (44). Chinese participants were graduate students in the US. Goh, Tan and Park (2009) say effects depend on stimulus composition.
agent_relevance: The famous perceptual-attention claim is shaky. Do not build an operator on 'East Asians look at context' as fact.

source: Klein, Lin, Radford, Masuda, Choi, Lien, Yeh, Boff (2009) Cultural differences in cognition: Rosetta Phase I, Psychological Reports 105
finding: A multi-country battery of six analytic-holistic tasks gave a mixed picture. Some tasks showed the predicted East-West gap, several did not, and two reversed.
numbers: N=379: Japan 94, Korea 92, Taiwan 99, USA 94. Exclusion task F(3,375)=11.56, p<.001: USA excluded more items than Japan (t186=3.74), Korea (t184=5.44), Taiwan (t191=4.89). Attribution Complexity composite: no difference. Categorization: holistic responses did not differ (F(3,181)=2.01, p>.05); only USA was slower (F(3,181)=7.14).
limits: Samples differed in age (F(3,375)=48.61) and education across sites. The authors say site differences added measurement error.
agent_relevance: In a six-task battery only about half behaved as predicted. A scaffold that applies one 'holistic' recipe will not generalise.

source: Klein, Lin, Radford, Masuda, Choi, Lien, Yeh, Boff (2009) Cultural differences in cognition: Rosetta Phase I, Psychological Reports 105
finding: Two classic tasks gave results opposite to prediction. On abstract syllogisms East Asians were more accurate than Americans. On concrete syllogisms Americans showed the larger belief bias.
numbers: Syllogism three-way interaction F(3,374)=5.35, p<.001, USA larger belief effects. Abstract accuracy F(3,375)=3.88, p<.01; Japan, Korea, Taiwan more accurate than USA (t186=7.06; t177.9=9.99; t191=6.96). Framed line relative-condition errors F(3,375)=16.92, USA least accurate.
limits: Authors call the framed-line and syllogism results hard to interpret because the USA sample differed in overall accuracy.
agent_relevance: Belief-bias versus logic is not safe to assign by culture. Apply the same logic check (G3) to every framing.

source: Klein, Lin, Radford, Masuda, Choi, Lien, Yeh, Boff (2009) Cultural differences in cognition: Rosetta Phase I, Psychological Reports 105
finding: The tasks barely agree with each other in the same people. Two verbal measures correlated weakly, and a perceptual task related to the verbal one at r=-.11 (not significant). Japan differed from Korea and Taiwan.
numbers: Attribution Complexity vs Exclusion r=-.14, p<.001. Facial expression magnitude vs Exclusion r=-.11, p>.05. N=379. Japan most sensitive to background faces (Shakiness F(3,375)=6.62, p<.001).
limits: Matches Na et al. (b05).
agent_relevance: East Asia is not one group. A cultural label is a poor switch for an agent's framing.

source: Ruan, Xie, Zhang (2014) Does rice farming shape individualism and innovation? A response to Talhelm et al. (2014), IFPRI Discussion Paper 01389
finding: A re-analysis of the rice-versus-wheat result (Talhelm et al. 2014). The original regressions replicated. After fixing sample imbalance, the holistic-thought (triad) result survived but implicit individualism weakened and loyalty/nepotism was fragile.
numbers: Implicit individualism N=515 (Fujian 142 = 27.57%; Qinghai 1; Shanghai 2). Loyalty/nepotism N=166 (three provinces with 1 observation). Dropping Fujian cut the rice coefficient for individualism from 1% to 10% significance. Holistic thought stayed highly significant after dropping oversampled provinces.
quote: After correcting these problems, most findings in the original paper no longer hold.
limits: A discussion paper, not peer reviewed (stated on cover). It also found rice provinces gained patents faster and had faster divorce growth, against the theory. Alternative collectivism measures showed no link.
agent_relevance: The triad holism result is the sturdiest of the three. The causal story about farming is weak.

source: Roberts (2015) Commentary: Large-scale psychological differences within China explained by rice vs. wheat agriculture, Frontiers in Psychology 6:950
finding: Galton's problem: provinces are not independent, so a rice-collectivism correlation may be inflated by shared history. Rice share tracks language ancestry.
numbers: Mantel test: difference in rice share correlated with linguistic distance, r=0.27, p=0.02 (10,000 permutations); 40 language varieties from 18 provinces.
limits: A commentary. It shows rice follows history; it does not show holism fails to follow rice.
agent_relevance: The causal explanation for the cultural split is unsettled. Treat 'holism is cultural' as a descriptive pattern only.

source: Experimental priming of independent and interdependent activity does not affect culturally variable cognition (2017) Royal Society Open Science
finding: Two lab experiments tried to move people toward analytic or holistic thinking by simulating solitary vs collective work. They did not move on seven analytic-holistic and self-construal measures in the predicted direction.
numbers: Experiment 1 n=84, Experiment 2 n=135, larger than 74% and 89% of the 104 experiments in the Oyserman and Lee (2008) priming meta-analysis. Only categorization showed an activity x time interaction, in the opposite direction, and it missed Bonferroni alpha=.007 (7 tests).
quote: We found no convincing evidence that either solitary or collective tasks affected any of the measures in the predicted directions.
limits: Authors warn the tasks may be inadequate, or that style is fixed early. Powered only for moderate to large effects.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that a short prime shifts thinking style. This cuts against cheap persona or role prompts as a style switch (consistent with G4).

source: Priming individualism/collectivism and eye movements for face recognition, West European/North American vs Chinese observers (2023) PLOS ONE
finding: Cultural differences in face scanning appeared between groups, but priming individualism/collectivism did not change them, and only some questionnaire subdimensions related to eye movements.
numbers: Two experiments. Conservative iMap4 analysis found no significant group effect; region-of-interest analysis showed wider fixation spread in Chinese observers.
limits: The Chinese sample came from a different region than earlier work, which may explain differences from prior findings. Sample sizes not recorded here.
agent_relevance: The perceptual difference is partly real but is not explained by the 'social orientation' mechanism the theory proposes.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The cultural psychology of large language models: is ChatGPT a holistic or analytic thinker? arXiv 2308.14242
finding: ChatGPT scored more holistic than the human norm on the Analysis-Holism Scale and the Triadic Categorization Task, but not clearly East or West on value scales.
numbers: Analysis-Holism Scale: GPT-3.5 M=5.35 (SD 0.11), GPT-4 M=5.01 (0.10), human norm 4.87 (SD 0.49, N=702), both p<0.001. Dialectical self: GPT-3.5 4.59 vs norm 4.00 (p<0.001); GPT-4 3.97 (p=0.344). Independent self-construal: GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32 vs norm 4.73. Triad task: GPT-3.5 0.87, GPT-4 0.85, above most Chinese provinces. 10 repeats per condition.
quote: ChatGPT consistently tends towards Eastern holistic thinking
limits: Self-report scales measure what the model says, not how it reasons. n=10 per cell, only OpenAI models. No link to task accuracy. GPT-3.5 answered at the scale ceiling (6.98 of 7).
agent_relevance: LLMs default to the holistic side on triad-style tests. So 'be more analytic' may be what the scaffold must add (O6).

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The cultural psychology of large language models: is ChatGPT a holistic or analytic thinker? arXiv 2308.14242
finding: The result held across temperature and prompt wording. Both models lean holistic on cognitive-process tests whatever the setting.
numbers: Temperatures 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, three alternative prompt sets, 10 repetitions each, 14 conditions per model. Authors report all findings robust (figure only, no table in text).
limits: No numeric robustness table in the text.
agent_relevance: Triad-style bias is a stable default of the model, so expect it to pull framing toward relations unless told otherwise.

source: Sabir, Gasper, Loem, Sharma (2025) Contrasting cognitive styles in vision-language models: holistic attention in Japanese versus analytical focus in English, arXiv 2507.00700
finding: Vision-language models describe images object-first (analytic) in English, and a bit more background-first (holistic) in Japanese. The Japanese shift is real but modest on ordinary images.
numbers: COCO 1K images: GPT-4o 22.6% holistic vs GPT-4o-JP 24.6% (balanced 6-shot 20.8% vs 26.1%). At 5K: 19.2-19.8% vs 23.6-28.6%. Random 1K COCO: GPT-4o 26.2%, GPT4o-JP 35.5%, Gemma-3-27B-JP 28.8%, Gemma-3-27B 19.2%, VILA-JP-14B 24.0%.
limits: 'Holistic' means the caption starts with background, a crude label from a classifier. Most captions are analytic in both languages. Human check of 200 captions by three native speakers: GPT4o-JP 17.75% holistic (model labels 29.0%), VILA-JP 15.33% (19.5%).
agent_relevance: Output language nudges framing order a little. It is a small lever, not a cultural switch.

source: Sabir, Gasper, Loem, Sharma (2025) Contrasting cognitive styles in vision-language models: holistic attention in Japanese versus analytical focus in English, arXiv 2507.00700
finding: Content mattered more than language: Japanese cultural images raised the holistic share far more than the language did. Back-translating captions shifted labels too.
numbers: Japanese cultural image set: GPT-4o-JP 73% holistic, up 47 points from COCO. On the 1K Japanese set GPT4o gave 59.1% and 57.6% (5- and 6-shot) holistic. Back-translation shifted the holistic/analytic ratio by 13.21% on average, with about 10% reversion.
limits: VILA-JP, trained on Japanese data, was not more holistic than GPT-4o-JP, so training language is not the whole story. Single labelling method.
agent_relevance: The scene decides the framing. A scaffold should pick framing from the problem, not from a cultural persona.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs, arXiv 2601.17096
finding: A 2x2 design (US vs Chinese model, English vs Chinese prompt) across eight tasks found model origin did not predict human-like cognitive patterns. On relational-versus-categorical pairing the US model was more relational than the Chinese model.
numbers: GPT-4o vs ERNIE 4.5, 100 runs per cell per task (400 per task), temperature 1. Categorization (relational minus categorical): US M=8.10 (SD 1.44) vs Chinese 6.04 (1.54), d=1.38, p<.001, opposite of the human East Asian pattern. Scene-description object count: Chinese model 12.31 vs US 8.66, d=2.42 (matches humans). Landscape drawing objects: DALL-E 3 11.53 vs iRAG 8.10, d=1.01 (opposite).
limits: Two chat models and two image models. Scoring used LLM judges (DeepSeek-V3, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen-VL-Max). Preprint, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Model origin is a poor predictor. Do not expect a 'Chinese' model to bring holism.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs, arXiv 2601.17096
finding: Prompt language did not reliably switch cultural style. English prompts sometimes gave the more 'East Asian' result (cultural reversal), and effects varied by model.
numbers: Chinese model on categorization: relational score 5.30 in Chinese vs 6.78 in English, t=-7.74, p<.001. Scene description objects: English 10.91 vs Chinese 10.07, p<.001. Attribution: Model x Language interaction F(1,396)=18.21, p<.001; the US model did not respond to language.
limits: Same limits as above. Compare b17, where Japanese output gave a small rise in holistic ordering. Results differ between tasks and models.
agent_relevance: Language-based frame switching is unreliable. For a different framing (O8), instruct the framing directly rather than translating.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs, arXiv 2601.17096
finding: The Chinese model attributed more to collective causes AND more to individual causes than the US model, which does not happen in humans (humans trade off). Safety alignment produced zero-variance answers on some tasks.
numbers: Collective attribution: Chinese model M=3.17 vs US 2.81, d=1.14; individual attribution 4.75 vs 4.67, d=0.27, p=.007. Ideal-affect task, Chinese model with English prompt: mean 5.00, SD 0.00, 100% at ceiling.
limits: The authors' reading ('service persona camouflage') is an interpretation, not tested against base models.
agent_relevance: Models do not carry a human trait structure. Test any style operator on a measured outcome rather than assuming it works by analogy (G3).

source: Masuda and Nisbett (2001) Attending holistically versus analytically: comparing the context sensitivity of Japanese and Americans, JPSP 81
finding: Cited as the founding perceptual study: Japanese described more background and relationships in underwater scenes than Americans.
numbers: Numbers not read this session. Do not rely.
limits: Evans et al. (b07) failed to replicate the related eye-tracking claim. Sabir et al. (b17) cite this work as motivation.
agent_relevance: Source of the idea that framing order differs. Treat as a hypothesis for LLM tests.

source: Talhelm, Zhang, Oishi, Shimin, Duan, Lan, Kitayama (2014) Large-scale psychological differences within China explained by rice versus wheat agriculture, Science 344
finding: Rice-growing provinces scored more holistic on the triad task than wheat provinces among Han Chinese participants (search record says 1,162 participants).
numbers: N about 1,162 per a search summary, not verified. About 303 citations at lookup.
limits: Re-analysed by Ruan et al. (b11) and questioned for non-independence by Roberts (b12).
agent_relevance: See b11 and b12.

source: Oyserman and Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Effects of priming individualism and collectivism, Psychological Bulletin 134
finding: This meta-analysis of 104 priming experiments is the benchmark cited by the 2017 priming study. It reports that priming individualism or collectivism affects cognition; b13 failed to find that for thinking style.
numbers: 104 experiments per the 2017 paper. Effect sizes not read.
limits: Not opened; seen only through b13.
agent_relevance: Backs the idea that framing can be induced, with the caveat from b13.

source: Multi-country study of analytic vs holistic tests (nearly 1,000 participants, 11 countries), source unidentified
finding: A press summary reported no clear East-West divide on tests of analytic vs holistic thinking in nearly 1,000 people across 11 countries.
numbers: About 1,000 participants, 11 countries, from a search snippet. Title, authors, effect sizes not verified.
limits: Only a press line seen. A lead to follow up, not evidence.
agent_relevance: If confirmed it would be the largest failed-replication signal. Needs a source check before use.

source: Czech preregistered validation of six analytic-holistic measures (2021-2023)
finding: A preregistered study of six measures on 392 Czech participants found questionnaires and rod-and-frame tasks may be unreliable, with poor factor structure and a link to intelligence. The authors proposed a three-level model.
numbers: N=392 per a search summary. Full text not opened (403).
limits: Single country, not cross-cultural.
agent_relevance: Supports b05: the tasks measure different things. Treat analytic-holistic as several skills, not one dial.
